strategyPosture: Stay selective and staged into the Oct 14 CPI. Credit is loose (SLOOS 0%, HY OAS 3.09%), VIX is 14.84, and the index is near its high, so there is no confirmed rollover to de-risk against — but a 5.6% 30-year and rotating leadership argue for owning the verified dislocations (AVGO-grade fundamentals at sentiment prices) rather than chasing extended momentum (PLTR +25.8% in one month, HIMS +10.23% in a day) or catching the speculative nuclear/space unwind.

themes.counterRead: This combination — index near highs, leadership diverging, credit loose — reads as rotation rather than a confirmed broad top, per the concentration model itself. But the divergence is real: if the gap widens while credit starts confirming, the read flips. Position for churn in leadership, not for index collapse.
themes.dataAnchor: Mag7 names average 9.33% below their 52-week highs versus SPY at 0.4% — an 8.93-point divergence gap. AAPL is the strongest Mag7 name at 2.5% off its high; TSLA the weakest at 23.3%. Bank lending standards are LOOSE (SLOOS 0%, far below the ~40% stress threshold), HY OAS sits at 3.09%, and VIX is 14.84, down 16.82% over one month — credit and volatility both refuse to confirm a rollover.
themes.label: Rotation, Not Rollover
themes.narrative: The index looks calm on a Saturday-morning read of Friday's close — SPY at $778.57, up 0.6% on the day and only 0.4% below its 52-week high — so the surface read is that nothing is wrong. Underneath, the names that carried the index are well off their own highs and leadership keeps rotating into new names like PLTR (+25.8% over one month).
themes.watchFor: Divergence gap: narrowing from 8.93 pts means rotation healing; widening past ~12 pts with HY OAS above 3.50% means rollover risk.

themes.counterRead: The split is the information: the unwind is narrative-ahead for the story stocks, whose declines are sentiment-driven and can extend, and data-ahead for the quality names sold with the theme. Lumping VST, BWXT, SMR, and ASTS into one 'nuclear trade' is now the error — the tape itself has stopped doing it.
themes.dataAnchor: Holding VST is up 9.5% over one month and 3.13% today, even while sitting 25.6% below its 52-week high on a PARTIAL_SIGNAL sentiment-driven tag, RSI 64.4. The speculative leg keeps falling: SMR is down 29.58% in one month, ASTS down 14.99% in one month and 10.54% today alone, URA down 13.8%, OKLO down 13.04%. BWXT sits between the two — 40.5% below its high while revenue grows 18.3% YoY with positive FCF ($185M), scored 77 (Tier B) by the screen.
themes.label: AI Power Bifurcates: Contracted vs Speculative
themes.narrative: The market is no longer trading AI power as one complex. Contracted, cash-generative power is being bought while the speculative nuclear and space names are still being unwound as story stocks with no fundamental anchor in the current data.
themes.watchFor: SMR/OKLO posting two consecutive positive weeks after -29.58%/-13.04% months would mark capitulation ending; VST losing its positive 1-month trend would say the bifurcation is closing from the wrong side.

themes.counterRead: Fundamentals and price moving in opposite directions is the definition of the setup, but it is not a timing signal by itself. A 5.6% 30-year caps the multiple the market will pay for even this growth, so the discount can persist until the rate path or the next print forces a re-rate.
themes.dataAnchor: AVGO is the screen's top conviction name (score 81, Tier A): revenue growing 55% YoY, gross margin 67.8%, free cash flow $26,914M at a 42.1% FCF margin — while the stock sits at $361.54, 27% below its 52-week high, RSI 50.1, tagged FULL_SIGNAL with a SENTIMENT_DRIVEN decline reason. The semi-equipment layer underneath confirms recovery rather than rollover: AMAT has a +11.7% one-month trend and KLAC +10.4%, both on MULTIPLE_COMPRESSION decline tags; CLS revenue grows 28.5% YoY and VRT 27.7% YoY.
themes.label: AI Infrastructure Quality at a Discount
themes.narrative: The tape is pricing Broadcom like a cyclical that already peaked — sold off with the AI complex on a sentiment-driven decline signal despite no fundamental break in the data.
themes.watchFor: AVGO holding above its recent range low while revenue growth stays near +55% YoY at the next print; a revenue deceleration would close the fundamentals-ahead-of-price gap from the wrong side.

themes.counterRead: Tight credit plus a steep curve is a multiple-compression regime, not a recession signal — it punishes long-duration cash flows (small caps, unprofitable growth) while cash-generative quality holds up. The risk is a hot CPI on Oct 14 pushing the 30-year through 5.6% and turning compression into a broader de-rating.
themes.dataAnchor: The curve stays bear-steep: DGS2 4.77%, DGS10 5.24%, DGS30 5.6%, 2s10s +0.47, real 10-year 2.89%, breakeven (T10YIE) 2.35%. HY OAS at 3.09% says credit disagrees with any stress story. The casualty remains duration-sensitive breadth: IWM is -3.09% over one month and -6.2% over three while SPY is +2.74%/+3.57% and QQQ +6.02%/+3.89%. Fed funds (DFF) sit at 3.88% with FOMC decisions on Oct 27-28 and Dec 8-9 ahead.
themes.label: The Long End Is the Pressure Point
themes.narrative: The market's anxiety is inflation and duration — event headlines flag 'inflation jitters' into the September CPI on Oct 14 — not credit or growth collapse. Equities rose into that print anyway on Friday: SPY +0.6%, QQQ +0.51%, and even IWM +0.45% on the day.
themes.watchFor: September CPI on Oct 14: DGS30 holding at or below 5.6% keeps the compression contained; a push through 5.75% with HY OAS widening past 3.50% changes the regime.

themes.counterRead: Depth of drawdown is not evidence of value — some of these declines are the market correctly repricing slower futures, and the screen does not separate those from sentiment overshoot. This is a research queue, not a buy list: each name needs its thesis verified before sizing, exactly as the posture flag in the data states.
themes.dataAnchor: The dislocation screen flags FULL_SIGNAL sentiment-driven declines in names whose revenue still grows: APP is 62.5% below its high at $277.04 with 76% gross margin and $3,480M FCF at a 60.8% margin (score 77, Tier B, RSI 35.4, watchlist promotion score 70 with RECOVERY inflection); NOW is 27% below its high with revenue +23.1% YoY (watchlist score 70, RECOVERY); HUBS is 54.2% below its high; TTD is 78.1% below its high with revenue +18.5% YoY and RSI 35.1; NXT is 47.2% below its high with revenue +20.3% YoY. The pullback posture in the data is RESEARCH_SCREENED — every candidate passed the 5-gate screen, but the screen verifies dislocation, not thesis.
themes.label: Dislocated Quality Growth
themes.narrative: A broad set of former growth leaders has been written off as broken — software and platform names sit 27-78% below their highs and the market is pricing them as structurally impaired.
themes.watchFor: Names from this screen printing revenue re-acceleration on their next reports while holding above post-decline bases; continued estimate cuts on the same names would confirm the impairment read instead.

watchFor: September CPI on Oct 14 — DGS30 (now 5.6%) holding at or below 5.6% vs pushing through 5.75%
Mag7-vs-SPY 52-week-high divergence gap narrowing from 8.93 pts (rotation healing) or widening past ~12 pts (rollover risk)
HY OAS staying at or below ~3.25% (credit calm) vs breaking above 3.50% (credit confirming stress)
AVGO holding its recent range while revenue growth prints near +55% YoY — the data-ahead test case
SMR/ASTS two consecutive positive weeks after -29.58%/-14.99% months — capitulation signal for the speculative power/space complex
whereWaveBuilds: The next move builds on the rate path into September CPI (Oct 14) and the Oct 27-28 FOMC: a soft print relieves the long end and re-rates the dislocated quality growth first; a hot print extends multiple compression, with IWM (-6.2% over three months) as the pressure gauge and the AI-power bifurcation widening.
